XIII.}}</noinclude>seeth me, seeth him that sent me. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=46}}† I a light am come into this vvorld: that euery one vvhich beleeueth in me, may not remaine in the darkenesse. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=47}}† And if any man heare my vvordes, and keepe them not: I doe not iudge him. for I came not to iudge the vvorld, but to saue the vvorld. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=48}}† He that despiseth me, & receiueth not my vvordes, hath that iudgeth him. the vvord that I haue spoken, that shal iudge him in the last day. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=49}}† Because of my self I haue not spoken, but the Father that sent me, he gaue me commaundement vvhat I should say, and what I should speake. {{verse|chapter=12|verse=50}}† And I knovv that his commaundement is life euerlasting. The things therfore that I speake: as the Father said to me, so doe I speake.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XII.}}}}

''5. Why vvas.'') So wicked, couetous, and sacrilegious persons reprehend good men for bestowing their goods vpon Church ornaments &c. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Church ornaments.}}vnder pretence of better bestowing them on the poore. such prouide for the poore as Iudas did.

''6. A theefe.'') Iudas did not then first perish when he sould our Lord, for he was a theefe before: and being lost he yet folowed Christ, not in hart, but in body onely. Which our Maister tolerated, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Toleration of the euil.}}to giue vs a lesson to tolerate the il, rather then deuide the body. ''Aug. tract. 50 in Io''.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XIII.}}}}}}

{{c|''At his last supper, to giue his farevvel, and that in most vvonderful louing maner, 4 he washeth his Disciples feete, 6 beginning vvith Peter, 8 (shewing hovv necessarie it is for vs to be washed by him in Baptisme, and needful also after Baptisme) 12 and by this example teaching them al humilitie one tovvard an other. 21 Then he foretelleth, that (notwithstanding his exceding loue tovvard them) one euen of them vvil betray him, meaning Iudas, 22 as to Iohn he secretly shevveth. After whose going out, he reioyceth and saith that euen now the houre is come, 34 commendeth vnto them to loue together, as a nevv commaundement, 36 and foretelleth Peter vvho presumed to much of his ovvne strength, that euen this night he vvil deny him thrise.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, scrolling foliage with grotesque heads.png|imgsize=140px|fl={{verse|chapter=13|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 26, 1. Mr. 14, 1. Luc. 22, 1.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō Maundy thursday at Masse, and at the washing of feete.}}before the festiual day of Pasche, {{sc|Iesvs}} knovving that his houre was come that he should passe out of this vvorld to his Father: vvhereas he had loued his {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=MAVNDY THVRSDAY.}}that vvere in the vvorld, vnto the end he loued them. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=2}}† And vvhen {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ By supper, he meaneth the eating of the Paschal lambe. for, the institution of the B. Sacrament was after this.}}∷ supper vvas done, vvhereas the deuil novv had put into the hart of Iudas Iscariote the sonne of Simon, to betray him: {{verse|chapter=13|verse=3}}† knovving that the Father gaue him al things into his handes, and that he came from God, and goeth to God: {{verse|chapter=13|verse=4}}† he riseth from {{hws|sup|supper,}}<noinclude>{{rh|||per}}</noinclude>
